scripts.build: wrangler types && astro check && astro build && npm run gate:content
scripts.//gate:app-css: QUAL-03, and it IS in gate:content because it is offline, source-scoped and reads 30 files in well under a second - the same shape as gate:ds and gate:sinks. Its operational definition of "confined to layout" (the application ARRANGES or HANDS A TOKEN THROUGH; it never ORIGINATES a value in a dimension the design system already names) is argued at length in the file header, along with the one exclusion worth arguing with: spacing, because DS-11 records that brand themes do not own it and the density axis does not exist until Phase 06.1. It ships with FOUR REGISTERED DEBTS - real violations it found and could not fix without taking a design decision - and prints all four on every PASS.
scripts.gate:content: npm run gate:schema && npm run gate:sinks && npm run gate:ds && npm run gate:app-css && npm run gate:photo-date && npm run gate:exif && npm run gate:photo-order && npm run gate:origin && npm run gate:public-js && npm run gate:fonts && npm run gate:placeholders && npm run gate:ladder
scripts.//gate:og-live: SEO-01. NOT chained into `gate:content`, and that is argued rather than defaulted: gate:content is eleven OFFLINE gates inside `npm run build`, so a network call there lets a CDN blip or an aeroplane red a build whose code is fine - which teaches a developer to re-run rather than to read. It runs in the two places where the network is ALREADY a precondition, so it adds no new class of failure: its own named CI step (a per-push question - does the artefact THIS push produced point at live images?) and the ship path, before `wrangler deploy`. It fetches with GET, not HEAD, because the question is what a CRAWLER gets; see the file header for why that is the opposite of `gate:liveness`'s measured choice and why both are right.
scripts.//gate:masters: The blocking prerequisite for the apex domain (roadmap Phase 8). The unwatermarked 2000px masters live at `private/<category>/<slug>-clean.webp` in the SAME bucket the site serves from, so `private/` is a path convention and not a permission boundary - 39 of 39 were MEASURED reachable on 2026-08-26. Closed by a Cloudflare WAF custom rule that exists only in a dashboard, which is why this fetches the real URLs rather than trusting it is still switched on. NOT chained into `gate:content` for the same reason `gate:og-live` is not: that is eleven OFFLINE gates inside `npm run build`, and a network call there lets a CDN blip red a build whose code is fine. It runs where the network is already a precondition - its own CI step, and the ship path before `wrangler deploy`. Its anti-vacuity control is the point of the file: a known-public image must answer 200 first, or every private URL failing to return 200 would report the masters sealed while proving nothing.
scripts.//gate:liveness-placement: `gate:liveness` sweeps all 160 manifest URLs with HEAD and asks whether the BUCKET still holds every object. That is a MONITORING question, not a per-push one - its answer changes for reasons unrelated to the commit - so it runs on the ship path (below) rather than on every push, where it would return the same answer twenty times a day for a corpus that changes only when the pipeline runs. 12.7s for 160 URLs, measured.
scripts.deploy: npm run gate:deps && npm run build && npm test && npm run gate:content && npm run gate:liveness && npm run gate:og-live && npm run gate:masters && wrangler deploy
scripts.//audit:public: JSON has no comment syntax, so the reason lives in this sibling key. `audit:public` is NOT chained into `npm test` or `npm run build`, and that is a decision: it needs a ~130 MB Chromium binary that no gate can install for you, and a browser measurement is deterministic PER MACHINE, not per platform - libvips, font rasterisation and sub-pixel layout all diverge on darwin/arm64 against ubuntu/x64, so a cross-platform pixel assertion is a flake generator. Phase 8 owns whether any of it becomes a CI gate under QUAL-01 and QUAL-04. Run `npx playwright install chromium` once, then `npm run build && npm run audit:public`.
scripts.//audit:lighthouse: Also NOT chained into `npm test` or `npm run build`, for the same reason as `audit:public`: a Lighthouse score is deterministic PER MACHINE, not per platform, and it fetches the 39 gallery photographs from the real image origin. It needs a Chrome; it uses Playwright's pinned Chrome for Testing, so `npx playwright install chromium` once is the same prerequisite the six-class audit already has. Run `npm run build && npm run audit:lighthouse`. Reports land in the gitignored `lighthouse-report/`.
